title: The Man Who Sold His Happiest Memory
style: Cozy Storytelling: warm painterly 2D environments and expressive minimalist characters
aspect_ratio: 16:9, center-safe staging for optional later portrait adaptation
timing_status: Editorial targets only. Actual original-speed narration must be measured before final shot timing and subtitles.

episodes.title: The Price of Happiness
episodes.payoff: Milo discovers the bargain is real.
episodes.ending: That evening, his sister found the receipt. Her smile vanished. Of all the afternoons, she whispered, you sold the last one we had together.

episodes.title: No Refunds
episodes.payoff: He learns that money cannot simply reverse the sale.
episodes.ending: Milo reached for the old receipt beneath it. The memory was called My Son's First Breath. His father had sold it twenty years ago.

episodes.title: The Second Customer
episodes.payoff: Their father's transaction opens a larger mystery.
episodes.ending: A stranger's childhood flickered across the wall. The buyer laughed at a father's joke. Milo recognized the crooked drawing. Someone was watching his afternoon.

episodes.title: Someone Else's Happiness
episodes.payoff: Milo moves from regret to action.
episodes.ending: His sleeve caught a tiny jar on the shelf. It fell. The seal cracked. Somewhere outside, a woman began to cry with relief.

episodes.title: The Broken Seal
episodes.payoff: The siblings discover a way to return the stolen moments.
episodes.ending: Beside the furnace stood their father's auction file. Inside was a hospital invoice. The patient was not their father. The patient was Milo.

episodes.title: What Dad Paid
episodes.payoff: The emotional midpoint reveals the father's sacrifice.
episodes.ending: He reached for the seal. Footsteps stopped behind them. The buyer was watching. He said the jars were his now, and locked the door.

episodes.title: Two Jars or Everyone
episodes.payoff: A personal escape becomes a choice to help others.
episodes.ending: A hand caught the cart before it rolled. The keeper stood in the passage. He looked at the girl's drawing and whispered, My daughter.

episodes.title: The Keeper's Daughter
episodes.payoff: The apparent accomplice chooses to help.
episodes.ending: Behind them, the loading door slammed open. The buyer saw the escaping cart, grabbed a shelf, and tipped it toward the furnace controls.

episodes.title: The Jar He Left Behind
episodes.payoff: The physical climax forces Milo's real choice.
episodes.ending: Milo stayed. The ceiling gave way. Behind the falling sparks, two small lights went dark. His father's beginning. Their last afternoon. Both gone.

episodes.title: What Was Still Here
episodes.payoff: The final episode pays off the loss and resolves the story.
episodes.ending: Then Lena knocked over her lemonade. The drawing was ruined. They looked at each other, and laughed. This time, Milo wasn't missing the moment.

scenes.narration: The first time Milo sold a memory, he asked if it would hurt. The shopkeeper said no. That was the first lie.
scenes.principal_picture: Rainy alley: Milo hesitates at an amber-lit shop; inside, the keeper slides one empty jar toward him.

scenes.narration: His rent was overdue. His drawing commissions had stopped. In his pocket, he had three coins and a key that might soon fit nothing.
scenes.principal_picture: Apartment doorway: eviction envelope beside sketchbook; count exactly three coins, then close Milo's hand around his key.

scenes.narration: The shop bought memories. A school prize paid almost nothing. A first kiss paid more. His happiest afternoon would cover the entire rent.
scenes.principal_picture: Shop counter: keeper compares three different jars and pushes a thick payment envelope forward. No generated labels.

scenes.narration: Milo chose a summer afternoon with his father. Two lemonades. A crooked drawing. His dad laughing so hard he could barely hold the pencil.
scenes.principal_picture: Warm memory: teenage Milo, younger Lena and their father at a kitchen table; two lemonades, crooked star drawing, shared laughter.

scenes.narration: A warm light slipped into the jar. Milo took the money. He remembered his father's face, but that afternoon had become an empty space.
scenes.principal_picture: Extraction counter: one warm light enters sealed jar; Milo receives envelope and loses the reflected memory, not his identity.

scenes.narration: That evening, his sister found the receipt. Her smile vanished. Of all the afternoons, she whispered, you sold the last one we had together.
scenes.principal_picture: Apartment kitchen: Lena holds receipt, points to the star drawing; match its shape to the memory, then hold on Milo's reaction.

scenes.narration: Milo had sold his last afternoon with Dad. The next morning, their father had gone into hospital. He had never come home.
scenes.principal_picture: Kitchen close-up: Lena opens an old photo beside the drawing; dissolve to an empty hospital chair, then return to Milo.

scenes.narration: He knew those facts. He could repeat them. But he could no longer remember the last time his father had made him laugh.
scenes.principal_picture: Milo studies the drawing and tries to recall; brief empty chair insert; his expression tightens without magical head effects.

scenes.narration: He ran back with the money. The keeper did not touch it. Sold memories belonged to the auction house until a collector bought them.
scenes.principal_picture: Night street into shop: Milo runs, sets intact envelope down; keeper refuses it and closes the auction ledger.

scenes.narration: At midnight, the jars would leave town. The sales were legal. The buyers were wealthy. And Milo could not afford his own happiness anymore.
scenes.principal_picture: Loading courtyard: numbered cases and auction invitation as post overlays; clock approaches midnight; distant elegant customers enter.

scenes.narration: Then he saw his jar on a packing cart. Beside it sat an older one, cloudy with dust, carrying his father's name.
scenes.principal_picture: Packing room through doorway: identify Milo's star-tagged jar beside one dusty jar bearing a distinct blue ribbon. Labels added in post.

scenes.narration: Milo reached for the old receipt beneath it. The memory was called My Son's First Breath. His father had sold it twenty years ago.
scenes.principal_picture: Receipt macro, composited readable title; Milo recognizes the date; cut to Lena entering behind him and seeing the same record.

scenes.narration: Their father had sold the moment Milo was born. Lena checked the date twice. It was not a mistake. Neither was the payment.
scenes.principal_picture: Shop service corridor: Lena compares receipt date with a childhood photo; Milo holds the blue-ribbon jar without opening it.

scenes.narration: The amount was enormous. Milo remembered a gentle man who patched his own coat. What could possibly have cost him that much money?
scenes.principal_picture: Memory of father mending coat; match the patched sleeve to a payment figure added afterward; return to the siblings.

scenes.narration: The keeper took the receipt away. Some people sell because they want more, he said. Some sell because someone else needs to live.
scenes.principal_picture: Keeper retrieves receipt carefully, looks toward a tiny faded family photograph behind the counter; Milo notices the glance.

scenes.narration: Before Milo could answer, a polished black car arrived. A buyer stepped out. The keeper straightened his coat and stopped looking at them.
scenes.principal_picture: Front window: black car pulls up; Collector enters in charcoal coat; keeper's posture changes; siblings retreat from view.

scenes.narration: Lena pulled her brother behind the shelves. Through a narrow doorway, they watched the buyer choose a memory and lower a glass viewing lens.
scenes.principal_picture: Archive aisle: Lena draws Milo into cover; through doorway, Collector fits one selected jar into an antique viewing device.

scenes.narration: A stranger's childhood flickered across the wall. The buyer laughed at a father's joke. Milo recognized the crooked drawing. Someone was watching his afternoon.
scenes.principal_picture: Projection room: cropped hand-drawn memory replay, Collector's entertained silhouette, Milo's furious eyes; no second physical father in present.

scenes.narration: A stranger was enjoying Milo's last afternoon with Dad. For the first time that night, being broke did not feel like the worst part.
scenes.principal_picture: Projection booth: Milo clenches his hand; Lena catches his wrist before he steps into the light; lens continues turning.

scenes.narration: The buyer called it charming. He asked whether the father had more memories available. The keeper said nothing. Milo nearly stepped out of hiding.
scenes.principal_picture: Collector gestures toward the projected father; keeper lowers his eyes; siblings remain concealed behind the shelving.

scenes.narration: Then the lens shut. The afternoon returned to its jar. Milo watched the keeper remove it and lock it inside a padded case.
scenes.principal_picture: Device close-up: lens closes, light returns to the sealed star jar; keeper places that single jar into the case.

scenes.narration: Lena had seen the key. She had also seen the delivery door. They could steal two jars, slip outside, and disappear before midnight.
scenes.principal_picture: Lena traces a route on a scrap of paper: key hook, case, courtyard door; Milo listens and nods.

scenes.narration: They waited for the keeper to follow the buyer. Then Lena lifted the key while Milo opened the case with both hands shaking.
scenes.principal_picture: Counter close-up: Lena lifts the brass key; packing room cut: she unlocks case as Milo opens its lid.

scenes.narration: His sleeve caught a tiny jar on the shelf. It fell. The seal cracked. Somewhere outside, a woman began to cry with relief.
scenes.principal_picture: One small jar falls from an adjacent low shelf; wax seal splits; warm light exits toward an older woman beyond window.

scenes.narration: The dropped jar had given its memory back. Outside, the woman pressed a hand to her mouth, remembering something she had thought was gone.
scenes.principal_picture: Courtyard window: older woman stops, touches her cheek and smiles through tears; match back to the empty cracked jar.

scenes.narration: Milo picked up the glass. It was empty. Breaking a seal released the memory to its original owner. Keeping it sealed kept it trapped.
scenes.principal_picture: Packing room floor: Milo raises the empty jar by its intact base; Lena notices the split wax and fading warm trail.

scenes.narration: They could free their two jars right there. Instead, Lena turned toward the shelves. Hundreds of other people's happiest days waited in the dark.
scenes.principal_picture: Lena's eyeline leads into rows of sealed amber jars; Milo holds his star jar and father's blue-ribbon jar, both still sealed.

scenes.narration: A school concert. A wedding morning. A quiet goodbye. The little tags made each jar sound small. Together, they looked like an entire town.
scenes.principal_picture: Archive inserts: visual symbols on tags, hands in memories behind glass; all readable descriptions composited in editing.

scenes.narration: Then they found the disposal chute. Broken glass went to a furnace. Its warning was simple: a burned memory could never be returned.
scenes.principal_picture: Rear workroom: closed furnace, chute and heat glow; a posted warning added in post; sister pulls Milo back from opening it.

scenes.narration: Beside the furnace stood their father's auction file. Inside was a hospital invoice. The patient was not their father. The patient was Milo.
scenes.principal_picture: Workroom desk: Lena opens invoice from blue-ribbon file; reveal a small childhood photo attached to it, then Milo's recognition.

scenes.narration: Milo had been sick as a baby. He knew the family story: a long hospital stay, a successful operation, a father who never complained.
scenes.principal_picture: Warm hospital memory: bundled infant Milo behind cot rails; father on waiting bench clutching a medical envelope; no graphic imagery.

scenes.narration: What nobody had told him was how the bill got paid. His father had walked into this same shop with nothing left to sell.
scenes.principal_picture: Earlier version of the same storefront: younger keeper receives father; rain and patched sleeve connect this moment to episode three.

scenes.narration: Except one thing. The first time his baby had gripped his finger. A tiny hand. A whole new life. His happiest memory.
scenes.principal_picture: Memory close-up: infant hand curls around father's finger; father bends close, stunned and tender; restrained camera move.

scenes.narration: He traded that moment for the operation. Then he went home and learned to love his son without remembering the moment he first had.
scenes.principal_picture: Father accepts payment, then returns to cot and takes child's hand again; establish a new present moment, not a restored memory.

scenes.narration: Milo looked at his own sealed jar. Dad had lost a beginning to give him a future. Milo had sold their ending for rent.
scenes.principal_picture: Present workroom: blue-ribbon jar beside star jar in Milo's hands; his shame shifts toward resolve as Lena steadies him.

scenes.narration: He reached for the seal. Footsteps stopped behind them. The buyer was watching. He said the jars were his now, and locked the door.
scenes.principal_picture: Collector appears in doorway; Milo shields both jars; Collector locks the outer workroom door, leaving an interior archive route accessible.

scenes.narration: The buyer locked them inside with the memories. He had seen the cracked jar. Now he wanted his shipment gone before they broke another.
scenes.principal_picture: Locked workroom: Milo tests outer door; beyond high window, Collector directs an empty handcart toward loading courtyard.

scenes.narration: Lena found a narrow service passage behind the shelves. At its end was the delivery hatch, wide enough for one person at a time.
scenes.principal_picture: Interior archive passage: Lena spots service route, opens low hatch to courtyard; no teleporting or new exit in locked door.

scenes.narration: They had a way out. Two jars. A clear street. Milo could go home with everything he had come to save that night.
scenes.principal_picture: Hatch viewpoint: safe courtyard beyond; Milo carries both jars; Lena crouches beside escape opening and waits.

scenes.narration: But on the shelf beside him was a jar tagged with a child's drawing. A little girl holding the hand of an older man.
scenes.principal_picture: Archive shelf close-up: a child-drawn family tag hangs from one pale pink-ribbon jar; Milo stops before the hatch.

scenes.narration: He put his jars in his satchel. Then he pulled an empty delivery cart toward the shelves. Lena watched him, sighed, and started loading.
scenes.principal_picture: Both hero jars go into Milo's ochre satchel; siblings load other sealed jars into a shallow padded cart, below its rim.

scenes.narration: A hand caught the cart before it rolled. The keeper stood in the passage. He looked at the girl's drawing and whispered, My daughter.
scenes.principal_picture: Keeper enters from accessible front archive route, stops cart by handle and recognizes pink-ribbon tag; leave both hands visible.

scenes.narration: The keeper recognized the drawing, but not the afternoon inside the jar. He had sold it years ago, when keeping the shop seemed worth anything.
scenes.principal_picture: Service passage: keeper studies tag with shame; his faded photograph matches the daughter shown in the child drawing.

scenes.narration: Over time, he had sold more. Her first song. Her ridiculous jokes. The sound of her coming home. He still knew her name.
scenes.principal_picture: Three brief bounded memory inserts show younger keeper and daughter; each fades back into separate sealed jars on shelf.

scenes.narration: But knowing a name, he said, was not the same as remembering a life. He had spent years protecting shelves he could not bear to empty.
scenes.principal_picture: Keeper's cramped office: family photograph behind ledger, warm jars reflected in his glasses; he closes the ledger and rises.

scenes.narration: He took the pink ribbon off the shelf. For a moment, Milo thought he would hide it. Instead, the keeper broke the seal.
scenes.principal_picture: Archive aisle: keeper lifts only pink-ribbon jar, twists wax stopper to break seal, keeps glass body intact.

scenes.narration: The old man's face crumpled into a smile. Then he unlocked the courtyard gate. Take the cart, he said. Take every jar you can.
scenes.principal_picture: Warm light reaches keeper; he unlocks courtyard gate from inside, then helps siblings push padded cart through the service hatch.

scenes.narration: Behind them, the loading door slammed open. The buyer saw the escaping cart, grabbed a shelf, and tipped it toward the furnace controls.
scenes.principal_picture: Workroom: Collector bursts through outer door he locked, yanks shelf in pursuit; metal frame strikes furnace control, sparks at panel.

scenes.narration: The falling shelf tore open the furnace chute. Hot glass spilled across the floor. A curtain caught fire. The passage filled with smoke.
scenes.principal_picture: Furnace workroom: broken chute opens, glowing debris hits curtain; smoke develops along ceiling, escape route still briefly visible.

scenes.narration: Outside, the keeper dragged the memory cart clear. Inside, Lena's coat caught beneath the fallen frame. Milo heard her call his name.
scenes.principal_picture: Courtyard: keeper pulls cart to safety; cut inside: Lena's sage sleeve trapped under metal frame, Milo turns back toward her.

scenes.narration: He pulled at the shelf. It would not move. He dropped his satchel, planted both feet, and lifted while Lena pulled herself free.
scenes.principal_picture: Milo places satchel on floor near doorway, braces feet and lifts one end of shelf; Lena withdraws trapped sleeve and crawls clear.

scenes.narration: They stumbled into the rain. Only then did Milo see his bag inside, beside the fire. His last afternoon with Dad was still in it.
scenes.principal_picture: Courtyard threshold: siblings emerge together; eyeline back to ochre satchel through smoky doorway; no hero jars elsewhere.

scenes.narration: He took one step toward the doorway. Lena reached for him. For a second, he held the hand that was here, and wanted what wasn't.
scenes.principal_picture: Close-up: Lena catches Milo's hand; camera holds both living hands, then rack focus to the satchel beyond the unsafe threshold.

scenes.narration: Milo stayed. The ceiling gave way. Behind the falling sparks, two small lights went dark. His father's beginning. Their last afternoon. Both gone.
scenes.principal_picture: Milo turns fully toward Lena; seen from safe courtyard, roof section collapses over satchel and two enclosed lights extinguish; no graphic injury.

scenes.narration: Milo saved his sister. He could not save the jars. By morning, the shop was ash, and the cart stood untouched across the street.
scenes.principal_picture: Dawn courtyard: firefighters in distant simplified silhouettes, contained ruins; padded cart safe across street with keeper and siblings.

scenes.narration: They broke the seals one at a time. Warm lights rose above the rooftops. Across town, people stopped in doorways and remembered their own lives.
scenes.principal_picture: Siblings and keeper open surviving jars individually; warm lights travel toward homes, wedding ring, school piano and hospital bedside.

scenes.narration: The keeper's daughter arrived before noon. He remembered her terrible jokes now. She told another. He laughed before she reached the ending.
scenes.principal_picture: Quiet street bench: adult daughter in rose cardigan sits with keeper; his recognition and laugh answer episode eight's absence.

scenes.narration: The buyer demanded his property. Lena told the officers who had locked them inside. They took him aside. His money couldn't answer their questions.
scenes.principal_picture: Ruined storefront exterior: Collector reaches for empty case; Lena identifies him to two briefly visible officers, who lead him aside for questioning.

scenes.narration: That evening, Milo opened his sketchbook beside Lena. He tried to draw their father laughing. The face came easily. The afternoon did not.
scenes.principal_picture: Apartment kitchen: Milo sketches father's face, pauses at empty background; Lena sits beside him with two lemonades and a clean page.

scenes.narration: Then Lena knocked over her lemonade. The drawing was ruined. They looked at each other, and laughed. This time, Milo wasn't missing the moment.
scenes.principal_picture: Lemonade spills over fresh crooked drawing; shared stunned glance becomes whole-body laughter; settle on hands and new drawing, warm light, final cut.
